claims.claim: The query is an aryloxypropanolamine beta-blocker-like molecule with a tert-butylamino group and an aryl ether; timolol, which shares the tert-butylamino aryloxypropanolamine core, has reported oral bioavailability of 50-75% in humans.

Metoprolol, another aryloxypropanolamine beta blocker, showed systemic availability of 84 ± 10% in cirrhotic patients, and propranolol in cirrhosis showed F values of 54-79%, all above the 20% threshold.
Other transferable contexts also place oral bioavailability at or above 20%: flecainide 70-95%, encainide 76-78%, and cocaine 32-45% with a retrospective range of 0.20-0.60.
No visible L1 record provides affirmative evidence for F < 20%; the mixed physicochemical prior based on ionization and TPSA is not endpoint proof of low bioavailability.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself is present; transfer is inferred from structurally related beta-blocker contexts.
First-pass metabolism and clearance of the query's urea-containing aryloxypropanolamine are not directly measured.
The query has no reported external condition, so cirrhosis or fed/fasted context matching is indirect.
The physicochemical prior is mixed due to ionization (neutral fraction 0.01) and TPSA 82.6, but these are not affirmative F < 20% evidence.
content.decision_summary: All visible L1 records from transferable beta-blocker and related contexts report oral bioavailability at or above 20%, mostly 50-100%; the query's aryloxypropanolamine tert-butylamine core aligns with timolol and metoprolol, so F >= 20% is better supported. Prediction: high.
